note: Doc 8168 — Core design criteria. — Procedures for Air Navigation Services — Aircraft Operations (Doc 8168), Volumes I (Flight Procedures) and II (Construction of Visual and Instrument Flight Procedures).

vi: Phương thức bay bằng thiết bị
note: Doc 8168 — SID, STAR, IAP, holding. — A series of predetermined manoeuvres by reference to flight instruments with specified protection from obstacles.

vi: Phương thức tiếp cận bằng thiết bị
note: Doc 8168 — 2D / 3D. — A series of predetermined manoeuvres by reference to flight instruments with specified protection from obstacles from the initial approach fix, or where applicable, from the beginning of a defined arrival route to a point from which a landing can be completed and thereafter, if a landing is not completed, to a position at which holding or en-route obstacle clearance criteria apply.

vi: Phương thức khởi hành chuẩn bằng thiết bị
note: Doc 8168 — Omnidirectional vs routed. — A designated IFR departure route linking the aerodrome or a specified runway of an aerodrome with a specified significant point, normally on a designated ATS route, at which the en-route phase of a flight commences.

vi: Phương thức đến chuẩn bằng thiết bị
note: Doc 8168 — Open vs closed STAR. — A designated IFR arrival route linking a significant point, normally on an ATS route, with a point from which a published IAP can be commenced.
Doc 8168 — May have holding. — A fix that marks the beginning of the initial segment and the end of the arrival segment, if applicable.
Doc 8168 — Alignment and speed reduction. — A fix that marks the end of an initial segment and the beginning of the intermediate segment.
Doc 8168 — Step-down possible. — A fix that marks the beginning of the final approach segment (non-precision / 2D).
Doc 8168 — Glide path intercept. — Point of an ILS/SBAS/GBAS precision approach at which the intermediate segment intersects the glide path.

Doc 8168 — Often navaid or waypoint. — Point in an IAP at or before which the prescribed missed approach procedure must be initiated in order to ensure the minimum obstacle clearance is not infringed.

Doc 8168 / Annex 6 — Precision / APV / LPV. — A specified altitude or height in a 3D instrument approach operation at which a missed approach must be initiated if the required visual reference to continue the approach has not been established.

vi: Độ cao hạ thấp tối thiểu
note: Doc 8168 / Annex 6 — Non-precision. — A specified altitude or height in a 2D instrument approach operation or circling approach below which descent must not be made without the required visual reference.

Doc 8168 — Basis for published minima. — The lowest altitude or the lowest height above the elevation of the relevant runway threshold or the aerodrome as applicable, used in establishing compliance with appropriate obstacle clearance criteria.

Doc 8168 — Preferred NPA technique. — A technique, consistent with stabilized approach procedures, for flying the final approach segment of a 2D instrument approach procedure as a continuous descent, without level-off, from an altitude/height at or above the FAF altitude/height.

Annex 6 / Doc 8168 — 3D with GP. — An instrument approach based on a navigation system that provides course and glide path deviation with minima as per operations specifications (typically ILS/MLS/GLS Cat I–III).
Annex 6 — 2D; fly CDFA. — An instrument approach based on a navigation system that provides course deviation but no glide path.

vi: Tiếp cận có dẫn đường thẳng đứng
note: Annex 6 / Doc 8168 — Baro-VNAV, LPV. — An instrument approach based on a navigation system that is not required to meet the precision approach standards but provides course and glide path deviation.
Annex 6 / Annex 10 — Standard precision. — DH not lower than 60 m (200 ft) and either visibility not less than 800 m or RVR not less than 550 m.
Annex 6 — Requires LVP. — DH lower than 60 m (200 ft) but not lower than 30 m (100 ft) and RVR not less than 300 m.
Annex 6 — Autoland typically. — A precision approach and landing with no DH or DH below 30 m (100 ft) and RVR less than 300 m, subdivided A/B/C.
Annex 10 — Typically 3.0°. — A descent profile determined for vertical guidance during a final approach.
Annex 10 — Front course / back course. — The component of ILS which provides course guidance to the runway centre line.
Doc 8168 — Typically 15–18 m. — The height of the ILS glide path / procedure path above threshold.

Doc 8168 — 45/180 or 80/260. — A manoeuvre in which a turn is made away from a designated track followed by a turn in the opposite direction to permit the aircraft to intercept and proceed along the reciprocal of the designated track.

Doc 8168 — Racetrack alternative. — A turn executed by the aircraft during the initial approach between the end of the outbound track and the beginning of the intermediate or final approach track. The tracks are not reciprocal.
Doc 8168 — Holding-pattern shape. — A procedure designed to enable the aircraft to reduce altitude during the initial approach segment and/or intercept the intermediate or final approach track.

Doc 8168 Vol II P4 — Entry: direct / parallel / offset. — A predetermined manoeuvre which keeps an aircraft within a specified airspace while awaiting further clearance. Standard: right turns, 1 min inbound ≤ FL140, 1.5 min above.
Doc 8168 — MOC 100%. — Area symmetrically disposed about the nominal flight track in which full obstacle clearance is provided.
Doc 8168 — Buffer. — Area along the outer edges of the primary area in which MOC reduces from 100% to 0%.

note: Doc 8168 — e.g. 300 m initial; 150 m intermediate; 75 m NPA final. — The minimum vertical clearance that must exist between aircraft and obstacles in the primary area of a segment.

Doc 8168 — Sectors / restrictions. — Departure procedure designed where no track guidance is provided.
Doc 8168 / Annex 14 — APV / PA alignment. — Obstacle protection surface for the visual segment of an approach.

Doc 8168 / Doc 9613 — MDA/H. — Lateral navigation only minima for RNP APCH (2D).
Doc 8168 — DA/H; temp limits. — Minima using Baro-VNAV vertical guidance with RNP APCH.
Doc 8168 / Doc 9613 — APV-I / APV-II. — Localizer Performance with Vertical guidance using SBAS.

Doc 8168 — Default. — Waypoint that requires turn anticipation so as to allow tangential interception of the next segment.
Doc 8168 — Used when fly-by not acceptable. — Waypoint at which a turn is initiated after overflying the waypoint.

note: Doc 8168 / Annex 10 — CRC protected. — Final Approach Segment data block for SBAS/GBAS approaches.

Doc 8168 — May be above OCA. — A published altitude/height flown operationally after considering obstacles, constraints and ATC.

Annex 19 — 5×5 matrix common. — The predicted probability and severity of the consequences or outcomes of a hazard.

Doc 9859 / EU 376/2014 — Enables reporting. — A culture in which front-line operators or others are not punished for actions, omissions or decisions commensurate with their experience and training, but where gross negligence, wilful violations and destructive acts are not tolerated.

note: Annex 13 / 19; national regs — CAA / ANS provider. — Required report of specified occurrences.

Ops / Doc 9966 — Day / swing / night. — A scheduled period of duty.

Doc 9966 — Jet lag / shift lag. — Endogenous ~24 h biological rhythm driving sleep propensity, alertness and many physiological functions.
Åkerstedt / Folkard models — CAS tools. — Circadian process in the two-/three-process model of alertness.

Three-process model — First 20–30 min after wake/nap. — Sleep inertia component in three-process models.
Doc 9966 — Controlled nap policy needed. — Temporary grogginess and performance impairment immediately after awakening.
Doc 9966 — Builds across night series. — Accumulated deficit relative to an individual’s sleep need.
Doc 9966 / some ANSPs — Not universally authorized for ATC. — Short sleep opportunity on duty under defined conditions (where permitted).

Scientific FRMS practice — Used in ATC roster design. — Operational fatigue score derived from circadian, sleep pressure and inertia components used in roster risk tools.

Åkerstedt — In-shift ratings. — 9-point subjective sleepiness scale widely used in FRMS.

Doc 9966 — At least one full night, often two after nights. — Sleep obtained after a duty sequence sufficient to restore baseline alertness.
FRMS science — Generally better tolerated than backward. — Shift pattern rotating day → evening → night (direction of clock).
FRMS science — Higher fatigue risk. — Night → evening → day rotation.
